result.title: InCue: Making Better Use of What Multimodal LLMs Already See at Test Time
result.summary: Even when multimodal large language models (MLLMs) answer incorrectly, their internal cues often point to the relevant region. A widely used remedy re-presents the cue-selected region as an enlarged crop to supply finer detail. However, we find that much of its gain requires no new detail: it largely survives when the crop comes from the already-seen low-resolution input, and partly even when the region's cached tokens are merely copied. Part of re-presentation's gain thus comes from drawing attention to evidence the model already holds. We propose InCue, a test-time framework that makes better use of this evidence without additional visual input. InCue treats visual attention and predictive-entropy gradients as Internal Cues, couples them into a spatial target, and optimizes only an offset on the existing visual tokens to steer attention toward it. Under matched visual-token budgets, InCue achieves state-of-the-art performance, consistently outperforming recent test-time methods and improving four MLLMs by up to 8.9% on V$^*$ and 23.4% on its hard samples. Its gains carry over to eight general benchmarks. Code will be available at https://github.com/paul-swu/InCue.

AI.brief_summary: 该文指出现有「放大裁剪区域」的收益大多不来自新细节，而来自把注意力引向模型已见的证据；据此提出 InCue，将视觉注意力与预测熵梯度耦合为空间目标，仅优化现有视觉 token 的偏移来重定向注意力，在多个 MLLM 与基准上取得提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「无需新增视觉输入、收益来自注意力重定向」的发现直接触及视觉细节保留与视觉旁路假设，且测试时的证据定位与视觉 token 偏移机制可供核查 LVR 中证据筛选与内部状态利用。
